rationale: This qualitative critical-geography case study conducts a historical and document analysis of the Detroit Water and Sewerage Department (DWSD) insolvency, interest rate swaps, and racialized narratives around residential water shutoffs. Its only quantitative content consists of secondary descriptive counts cited from news/advocacy sources (e.g., annual household shutoff totals on pp. 1 and 6), a reproduced swap schedule from a 2012 bond statement (Fig. 1, p. 5), and a descriptive accounting plot of DWSD net assets FY 2006–2014 with and without swaps/write-offs adapted from a 2015 consultant memo (Fig. 2, pp. 5–6). No inferential statistical models, hypothesis tests, effect estimates, standard errors, confidence intervals, or p-values are reported anywhere in the paper.
